newsitem.title: USA: Yukos Oil to choose investment banker by end-May.
newsitem.headline: Yukos Oil to choose investment banker by end-May.

text.p: Russia's Yukos Oil will choose an investment banker by the end of this month to help raise several hundred million dollars for expansion, the head of Yukos said on Wednesday.
Yukos is one of around a dozen vertically-integrated Russian oil companies created over the last few years. Its main production unit is Yuganskneftegaz.

Mikhail Khodorkovsky, chief executive officer of Yukos, said Russia's second-largest oil company planned to raise "in the hundreds of millions" in new funds as part of its strategy to complete a restructuring of the company by the end of 1997.
"We intend to acquire new oilfields. We intend to rebuild our refineries," Khodorkovsky told reporters. Yukos also wants to eventually expand, acquire and build new petrochemical plants, he said.
And the company would eventually "very much like" to participate in Russia's wholesale electricity market, he said.
Yukos has already received permission to issue American Depository Receipts for trading on U.S. exchanges, he said.
"We're also looking at the possibility of issuing secured and unsecured bonds," Khodorkovsky said. "And of course we're looking at garden variety bank borrowing."
He said Yukos would select an investment banker by the end of May, adding that several major U.S. companies were seeking the business.

Khodorkovsky, who was visiting the United States to try and line up financial partners, said he would meet with Amoco Corp. Yukos and Amoco are already in a partnership to develop the Priobskoye field.
"There is a need for us to continue further negotiations with Amoco," he said. "We have already begun the development of the Priobskoye field on our own."
Yukos is seeking partnerships with companies "that don't view us only as a handy source of raw materials"

Khodorkovsky, who is also chairman of Menatep, Russia's second largest bank, also said Yukos had hired Price Waterhouse to complete an audit of the oil company's books by September using western accounting standards.
"At the moment we are not exactly in 100 percent compliance with western (corporate) transparency standards," he said.
In response to a question, Khodorkovsky said Yukos welcomed international pressure on the Russian government to discourage bribery and corruption.
Yukos spends "over $100 million a year" on various payments and taxes to local, regional and federal government agencies in order to do business, he said.
"Those bureaucrats who siphon off money, who steal money, don't spend it in Russia. They spend it here," he said.
Yukos produced more than 33 million tonnes of oil last year.
